newsitem.title: JAPAN: S&P affirms Mitsui Fudosan's A2 rating.
newsitem.headline: S&P affirms Mitsui Fudosan's A2 rating.

text.p: Standard & Poor's Corp (S&P) said on Wednesday that it had affirmed its A2 rating for Mitsui Fudosan Co Ltd and its unit Mitsui Fudosan (New York) Inc.
The affirmation follows the company's announcement that it would write off non-performing assets worth 110 billion yen in the fiscal year ending March 31, 1997, S&P said in a statement.

The current rating reflects the attractive longer-term prospects of Mitsui Fudosan's business, which is supported by a strong franchise and good properties which enable it to maintain a relatively stable financial profile despite difficult industry conditions, it said.
Mitsui also enjoys strong financial flexibility thanks to its liquid assets, saleable buildings and subsidiaries and support from Mitsui Group companies, S&P said.

In 1996/97, Tokyo Disneyland operator Oriental Land KK, which is 38 percent owned by Mitsui Fudosan, will list on the Tokyo Stock Exchange. Mitsui Fudosan expects a capital gain of at least 27.6 billion yen from the listing, S&P said.
This will help offset the asset writeoff, and the company estimates a net loss of around 67 billion yen on a group basis for the year, S&P said.

The rating agency said the company's book debt leverage would not be significantly affected, as debt reduction from the sale of non-performing assets and proceeds from the Oriental Land stock offering would offset the decline in shareholder funds.
S&P said it views positively Mitsui Fudosan's more open and realistic disclosure of its situation and some acceleration in its programme to reduce debt.

With relatively thin debt coverage measures, Mitsui Fudosan remained exposed to further weakening in either its core development and sales business or the generally more stable leasing and management business, it said.
S&P said it would closely monitor property sales, leasing performance and Mitsui's progress toward its objective of reducing interest-bearing debt to one trillion yen by March 31, 1998.
